why: Details how to model unit economics to determine whether offering deep discounts is more profitable than paying higher Customer Acquisition Costs (CAC), using a mathematical breakdown of post-marketing contribution margins.

Topics. unit economics / Defining the Unit Economics Framework as the financial breakdown of a relationship with one single customer, including revenue, discounts, COGS, and profits. Evaluating the true cost of acquisition by adding the customer discount and the Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) together into one combined metric. Demonstrating mathematically that offering a $60 discount can yield the exact same $25 post-marketing contribution margin per customer as offering a $0 discount, provided the discount generates a proportional lift in website conversion rate (e.g., jumping from 1.5% to 3.8%) that equivalently lowers the CAC (e.g., dropping from $100 to $40). discount strategy / Managing discounts and marketing budgets as one combined financial pool rather than separate expenses. Recognizing that giving $100 to an advertising platform or giving $100 to a customer via a discount has the exact same profitability impact on a per-unit basis. Leveraging deep discounts strategically as an on-ramp into subscription or loyalty programs to guarantee high customer lifetime value (LTV), rather than wasting them on one-off flash sales. Maximizing total company profit by modeling which discount scenario yields the highest total volume of customers, showing how an optimized discount strategy can drive total company profit from $25,000 to $63,000 utilizing the exact same $100,000 ad spend.

Look for. The definition of Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): the average marketing or advertising invested to get one customer to buy for the very first time. The mathematical insight on discounts versus CAC: if a discount increases conversion rates enough to lower the CAC by the exact same dollar amount, the per-unit post-marketing contribution margin remains completely identical. The strategic rule for deep discounts: they should be explicitly attached to an on-ramp into a loyalty or subscription program rather than utilized for standard flash sales.
